stem: Which stage of adolescence is typically associated with the highest rates of risk-taking behaviour?
explanation: Middle adolescence is the stage most associated with peak risk-taking behaviour. Sensation seeking is high during this period, while frontal lobe regulatory control is still maturing.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because early adolescence is associated with pubertal change and increasing arousal, but peak risk-taking usually occurs later.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because middle adolescence is characterised by high sensation seeking and more complex thinking without full frontal lobe regulatory maturity.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because risk-taking often declines in late adolescence as executive control and self-regulation improve.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because early childhood is not the developmental stage typically associated with adolescent risk-taking behaviour.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because young adulthood generally has more mature executive control and less peak adolescent risk-taking.

source.hint: This phase occurs when cognitive ability is high but emotional regulation is still catching up.
